newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks end lower, snapping nine-day winning run.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks end lower, snapping nine-day winning run.

text.p: After nine consecutive winning sessions, Hong Kong share prices finally gave up some ground on Tuesday, ending weaker as stocks ran into profit-taking and the Hang Seng Index met resistance above 14,000 points.
The index fell 81.34 points, or 0.58 percent, to 13,906.46 after rising to an early high of 14,019.03.
Turnover was HK$15.23 billion compared with Monday's record HK$18.04 billion.
"There's a bit of profit-taking here. The index hit 14,000 and can't really go through with a bang so now it is coming off," said Geoff Galbraith, institutional sales trader at Nava SC Securities.
"The 14,000 level is sort of an invisible resistance point."
Hang Seng Index May futures rose 25 points to 13,930.
Miles Remington, sales trader at SocGen-Crosby Securities, said investors were not quite ready to push the Hang Seng Index decisively through the 14,000-point level yet.
"They think that probably 14,000 would have been overdone too quickly," he said.
But he added: "I think we will see 14,000 before too long."
The Hang Seng Index had gained 1,387.38 points, or 11.0 percent, during the previous nine sessions.
Brokers said the market was likely to be soft over coming days.
"The market has factored in an interest rate stalemate (in the United States) whereas there are still a lot of people out there who still see an interest rate hike," said Remington.
He said the market could be volatile next week ahead of the U.S. Federal Reserve's policy-setting meeting on May 20.
Among the blue chips, shares in HSBC Holdings Plc which led the market to its recent record highs, ran out of steam and ended HK$1.00 lower at HK$217.00.
Hongkong Telecom gained HK$0.10 to HK$15.20.
Brokers said some investors were expecting parent Cable & Wireless to make an announcement about its Hongkong Telecom stake when it releases its full-year results on Wednesday.

Trading in shares of China Everbright Technology was suspended on Tuesday, sparking speculation it would receive a stake in Hongkong Telecom. Its parent China Everbright Holdings has agreed to buy CITIC Pacific Ltd's 7.74 percent stake in Hongkong Telecom.
